events.title: Hanani Reports Jerusalem's Distress
events.description: At Susa in Artaxerxes's twentieth year, Hanani tells Nehemiah that the survivors in Judah are suffering disgrace and that Jerusalem's wall and gates remain ruined.

events.title: Nehemiah Prays for Jerusalem
events.description: Nehemiah mourns, fasts, and confesses Israel's sins before God. He appeals to the covenant promise of restoration and asks for favor before the king whom he serves as cupbearer.

events.title: Artaxerxes Commissions Nehemiah
events.description: The king notices Nehemiah's grief and grants him leave to rebuild Jerusalem. He supplies letters for safe passage and authorizes timber for the city gates, wall, and Nehemiah's residence.

events.title: Nehemiah Arrives in Judah
events.description: Escorted by royal officers and cavalry, Nehemiah presents the king's letters to the provincial governors and reaches Jerusalem. Sanballat and Tobiah resent his mission on Israel's behalf.

events.title: Nehemiah Inspects the Walls at Night
events.description: After three days in Jerusalem, Nehemiah secretly surveys the ruined walls and burned gates at night with a small group. He initially conceals his plans from the city's leaders and workers.

events.title: The People Commit to Rebuild
events.description: Nehemiah tells Jerusalem's leaders of royal support and urges them to end the city's disgrace by rebuilding. The people agree, while Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem mock the project and allege rebellion.

events.title: Families and Guilds Repair the Wall
events.description: Priests, rulers, artisans, merchants, families, and residents of nearby towns rebuild successive gates and wall sections around Jerusalem. Eliashib and the priests begin at the Sheep Gate, and the assignments continue around the city.

events.title: The Builders Resist Intimidation
events.description: Sanballat and Tobiah ridicule the builders as the wall reaches half its height, then a wider coalition plots an attack. The community responds with prayer and posts a continuous guard.

events.title: Nehemiah Arms the Wall Builders
events.description: With workers exhausted and enemies threatening surprise attack, Nehemiah stations armed families at vulnerable places. Work resumes under guard, with laborers carrying weapons and remaining inside Jerusalem overnight.

events.title: Nehemiah Confronts the Debt Crisis
events.description: Families protest that famine, taxation, debt, and enslavement are costing them their land and children. Nehemiah rebukes the nobles for exacting interest and binds them by oath to restore property and cancel their claims.

events.title: Nehemiah Waives the Governor's Allowance
events.description: During twelve years as governor, Nehemiah refuses the customary food allowance because of the people's burden. He supports a large household at his own expense, acquires no land, and continues working on the wall.

events.title: Nehemiah Refuses the Meetings at Ono
events.description: Sanballat and Geshem repeatedly invite Nehemiah away from the work and circulate an accusation that he plans to become king. Recognizing their intent to harm and frighten him, Nehemiah refuses to leave Jerusalem.

events.title: Nehemiah Rejects Shemaiah's Plot
events.description: Shemaiah urges Nehemiah to hide inside the temple from an alleged assassination attempt. Nehemiah recognizes that his opponents hired the prophet to frighten him into an act that could discredit him.

events.title: Jerusalem's Wall Is Completed
events.description: The wall is finished on the twenty-fifth day of Elul after fifty-two days of work, alarming the surrounding peoples. Tobiah nevertheless maintains influential family ties in Judah and continues sending intimidating letters.

events.title: Nehemiah Appoints Jerusalem's Guards
events.description: With the gates installed, Nehemiah appoints gatekeepers, singers, and Levites, places Hanani and Hananiah over Jerusalem, and establishes strict guarding procedures. He then prepares to register the sparsely populated city.

events.title: Nehemiah Reviews the Returnee Register
events.description: Nehemiah finds the genealogy of the first return under Zerubbabel and records its families, temple personnel, possessions, and gifts. People lacking proof of descent are restricted from priestly privileges pending a priestly ruling.

events.title: Ezra Reads the Law to the Assembly
events.description: The people gather at the Water Gate and ask Ezra to read the law. Levites explain it to the assembly, and the leaders turn the people's weeping into a communal celebration with provisions shared among those in need.

events.title: The Community Keeps the Festival of Booths
events.description: After leaders study the law, the returned community builds shelters throughout Jerusalem and observes the seven-day festival with great rejoicing. Ezra reads from the law each day, followed by a solemn assembly.

events.title: The Assembly Confesses Israel's Sins
events.description: The Israelites assemble in fasting and mourning, hear the law, and confess their own sins and those of their ancestors. The Levites recount God's care from creation through the patriarchs, exodus, wilderness, conquest, monarchy, exile, and the community's present subjection.

events.title: The Community Seals a Covenant
events.description: Nehemiah, priests, Levites, leaders, and the wider community bind themselves by a written agreement to obey the law. Their commitments address intermarriage, sabbath commerce, debt release, offerings, tithes, and support for temple service.

events.title: Jerusalem Is Repopulated
events.description: The leaders settle in Jerusalem, and lots select one in ten of the remaining people to join them, while volunteers are commended. A census records the city's residents and the communities occupied throughout Judah and Benjamin.

events.title: Priestly and Levitical Lines Are Recorded
events.description: A record traces priests and Levites from the return with Zerubbabel through later high-priestly generations. It also identifies leaders responsible for praise, thanksgiving, and guarding temple storehouses in Nehemiah's time.

events.title: Jerusalem's Wall Is Dedicated
events.description: Levites and singers gather for the wall's dedication after priests, people, gates, and wall are purified. Two thanksgiving processions circle the wall in opposite directions and meet at the temple for sacrifices and a celebration heard far away.

events.title: Temple Contributions Are Organized
events.description: Officials are appointed over storerooms for contributions, first fruits, and tithes. Judah provides the prescribed portions for priests, Levites, singers, and gatekeepers who conduct the temple service.

events.title: Nehemiah Returns to Artaxerxes
events.description: In Artaxerxes's thirty-second year, Nehemiah leaves Jerusalem and returns to the royal court. During his absence, Eliashib converts a temple storeroom for the use of his relative Tobiah.

events.title: Nehemiah Expels Tobiah from the Temple Rooms
events.description: After obtaining leave to return to Jerusalem, Nehemiah discovers Tobiah's quarters in the temple courts. He removes Tobiah's belongings, orders the rooms purified, and restores the sacred vessels and offerings.

events.title: Nehemiah Restores Support for the Levites
events.description: Nehemiah learns that unpaid Levites and singers have abandoned their posts for their fields. He rebukes the officials, restores the ministers to duty, resumes tithes, and appoints reliable treasurers.

events.title: Nehemiah Enforces Sabbath Rest
events.description: Seeing agricultural work and commerce on the sabbath, Nehemiah rebukes Judah's nobles and closes Jerusalem's gates to merchandise. He posts guards and assigns purified Levites to preserve the weekly rest.

events.title: Nehemiah Confronts Intermarriage
events.description: Nehemiah discovers Judeans married to women from neighboring peoples and children unable to speak Judah's language. He confronts the offenders, compels an oath against further marriages, and drives away a high priest's relative allied by marriage to Sanballat.

events.title: Nehemiah Orders the Priestly Service
events.description: Nehemiah purifies the community from foreign influence, assigns priests and Levites to their duties, and establishes regular provision for wood offerings and first fruits.
